July 24, 2019 Meeting Minutes

Commissioners
Michael Benbow  Chairperson

Staff Members
Peter Puglese  TE, PE, City Traffic Engineer

Diana Maximo  Serco Manager
Lieutenant Cardell Hurt  Traffic Unit Commander

1. Roll Call
   A meeting of the Parking and Traffic Commission was held at City of Inglewood’s Community Room located on
  the 1st Floor on July 26, 2019, at 19:07.
   All Commissioners and City Staff were present with the exception of Commissioner Barbara Brooks and Diana
  Maximo.

2. Approval of Minutes for July 24, 2019
   Motion to accept the meeting minutes was made by Commissioner Leonel Garcia
   Seconded by Commissioner Braggs
   4-1 approved Meeting Minutes

3. Public Comments (not listed on the agenda)
   Resident provided comments on speeding and shortage of parking on 110th West Street between Prairie Avenue and
  Doty Avenue. Resident then provided a speed hump and parking permit petition application. Lieutenant Cardell
  Hurt also provided information on who to call on these matters.

4. Unfinished Business
  a) None

5. New Business
   The Public Works (PW) Department explained the block party process and expressed the concern of not receiving
  barriers and barricades after a block party. The PW Department proposed to charge the applicant with a refundable
  deposit fee when applying for a block party. The Parking and Traffic Commission recommended that the PW
  Department proceeds with an investigation into how this refundable deposit fee can be implemented into the current
  block party program procedures.
   Public Works Department looked into the intersection of Fairview Blvd & La Tijera Boulevard. City Staff explained
  that the intersection was recently modified to improve visibility and reduce speeds.

6. Public Hearing
   None

7. Resolution
   None

8. Referral from City Council or City Department
   None

  Public Works Department

  MEMORANDUM
  July 24th, 2019

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission
FROM:  Public Works Department
SUBJECT:  Block Party Fees

BACKGROUND:
In May 2007, the Parking and Traffic Commission approved a resolution to adopt requirements and
procedures as a policy for the approval to barricade public streets for block parties. As a result of the
resolution, Public Works was able to standardize the requirements in which Block Party’s would be
approved or denied.

One of the roles Public Works plays in the Block Party process is supplying the Block Party Organizer
with a set of barricades and barriers. If the Block Party application is approved, Public Works drops off
the barriers and barricades on the last working day before the event to the Block Party Organizer for them
to setup the closure of the street on the day of the event. Public Works will then pick up the barriers and
barricades on the first working day after the event.

DISCUSSION:
Currently, the City does not charge a fee to process the permit, to use the City’s equipment or to deliver
and pick-up the equipment. The City of Inglewood has about forty-five (45) block parties on an annual
basis. Fourth of July is the largest and most requested events by the community, ranging from 18-20 block
parties for that day. Also, in addition to block parties, the City supplies barricades and barriers for events
approved by the Permits and Licencing Committee and other various requests by the Police and Fire
Departments. The timeframe for Public Works to prepare and provide the barriers and barricades for a
block party event is 72 hours before the event.

When Public Works delivers the supplies for the event, it usually includes four (4) long barricades with
eight (8) sawhorse legs (this may vary based on street size or access points to the closure). On special
request, Type 1A frames are also provided. This amount provides enough supplies for two (2) barricades
to be set up on each end of the street. Currently, Public Works owns 148 long barricades with 296
sawhorse legs. The table below breaks down the equipment cost loaned out for a block party event:

Equipment Description  Unit Price  Quantity  Total
1x8x10 longboard with sawhorse legs  $  60.00  4.00  $ 240.00
  $ 240.00

Throughout the Block Party program, there have been times that the barriers and barricades that Public
Works delivered to the resident are either not returned or returned damaged. The most common item

destroyed are the sawhorse legs, which Public Works either replaces or tries to fix. According to Public

To ensure the longevity of the Block party program and that the barriers and barricades will be delivered
back to the City and in good condition, other cities have implemented fees attached to the Block Party
application. These fees vary from non-refundable application fees, rental fees, and refundable deposits.
Below is a table of neighboring cities block party fees:

 City  Application Fee  Specific Barrier and Barricade Fee
 City of Inglewood  none  none
 City of Torrance  none  May ask for a deposit
 City of Hawthorne  $56 (non-refundable)  $200 deposit (refundable)
 City of Redondo Beach  None  None
 City of Gardena  $100 (non-refundable)  $100 deposit (refundable)
 City of El Segundo  $25 (non-refundable)  None
 City of Manhattan Beach  $50 (non-refundable)  $26/barricade (rental) + $112 damage fee
 City of Hermosa Beach  $198 (non-refundable)  none
 City of Santa Monica  none  $100/barricade + $50/sign deposit (refundable)
  The applicant will be billed for lost/damaged
 Culver City  none
  equipment

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission review the current City of Inglewood fee
structure to the surrounding neighboring City’s and provide Public Works with guidance on the following:
  1. Implementing a fee for the block party and usage of barriers and barricades?
  2. If so, What type of fee? (i.e refundable, non-refundable, rental, etc)

The Parking and Traffic Commission should consider the benefits and impacts it will have on the Block
Party Program.
